node_definition.done_when: No real scheduler verb runs at any point in this node. Every pytest run has, first on PATH, a shim directory under the run directory holding salloc, sbatch, srun, squeue, scontrol and scancel stubs. Each stub appends its argv and its caller's PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST to a log under the run directory, then exits non-zero. `squeue -u $USER -h -o '%i %j %M'` is logged before and after every run, and no job named reckon-reservation appears. First, the tests that reach a scheduler through dispatch are named. The candidate files are run one at a time under the shim: tests/test_dispatch_places_into_the_shared_reservation.py, tests/test_crew_placement.py, tests/test_crew_lane_agnostic_placement.py, tests/test_crew_workspace_requirements.py, tests/test_crew.py, tests/test_flight.py, tests/test_capabilities.py, tests/test_crew_binding_bound.py, tests/test_concurrency_bound_refuses_by_name.py and tests/test_landing_contract_follows_the_grant.py. The manifest lists every test id whose run logged a salloc or sbatch call, with the call path from dispatch to ensure_reservation at file and line in reckon/crew/dispatch.py and reckon/crew/placement.py. It also says why the recording scheduler that test already uses, if any, did not intercept the call. Five real allocations were minted this way on 2026-09-30, one per whole-suite run, each with partition all, 32 CPUs, 128 GB and an unlimited time limit. The fix has two parts. First, each named test gives its dispatch a recording scheduler, or a placement that never reaches the real one, and keeps its assertion. Second, tests/conftest.py fails any test that reaches a scheduler verb the test did not provide, and the failure names the verb and its argv. The check puts a failing stub first on PATH for the whole session, and a test's own recording scheduler, prepended later, still takes precedence. After the fix, the whole suite is run once with pytest-xdist -n 8, the shim in place and a per-test --basetemp under /tmp. The shim log records no salloc or sbatch call. Every failing id at head also fails at base, or the manifest attributes it. The negative control is executed and logged under the shim: with one named test's fix reverted in a scratch tree, the conftest check fails that test, naming salloc. No assertion is deleted. Every log sits under the run directory, headed with revision, tree and literal command, and ends EXIT=, and basetemps are deleted afterwards. tests/test_crew.py is run but not edited, because other nodes hold it. If a test there reaches a scheduler, the manifest names it under follow_ons with the one-line fix it needs, and the full-suite arm lists it as attributed. Only tests/conftest.py and the other named test files change, and the manifest lists which of them it edited.
